summary: Sequatchie County, TN: a lookout tower was planned in 1926 for a coal and lumber company; no build date found; Tennessee Landforms lists it standing; do not climb.

visit.trail_note: Tennessee Landforms advises against climbing these towers because steps are often removed or rotten; we found no public visiting arrangement

events.note: Planned, not confirmed built. A Kingsport Times report dated January 3, 1926, quoted by Forest Lookouts, describes a lookout tower of about seventy feet to be constructed on Jakes Mountain for the Rocky River Coal and Lumber Company, with about 13 miles of telephone line.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1926 newspaper report places Jakes Mountain in Van Buren County. Tennessee Landforms and the Division of Forestry form both list Sequatchie County, so the story follows the two later lists.

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, 1933 to 1975
sources.publisher: National Park Service (National Register multiple property documentation form)

notes_for_editor: Three sources only. No build date, staffing, fire record or current access arrangement was found. The 1926 item is a plan by a coal and lumber company and predates many Division of Forestry towers, so whether it was built is unknown. The county conflict (Van Buren in 1926 versus Sequatchie in the later lists) is recorded in resolved_conflicts. The standing status rests on one undated Tennessee Landforms list. The header of the Division of Forestry form's list was not readable, so we cannot say whether it covers only surviving towers. Two WebSearch calls were used; the results added nothing usable beyond the sources cited.
